captions.instagram:
How does a calculator work?

Press 7 and a chip scans a grid of wires, waits out the bounce and stores 0111. Build the adder from real logic gates, watch the carry ripple, and see why 1 ÷ 3 × 3 can come out as 0.9999999.

→ A pocket calculator: 20 keys, one chip, a display and a solar cell the size of a stamp.
→ Take it apart: keys on rubber domes, a grid of pads, one chip under black epoxy.
→ The chip lights one row at a time; a pressed key joins its row to a column.
→ Logic gates turn 1s and 0s into answers: AND needs both, OR needs either, XOR needs them different.
→ Inside each gate: transistors as switches. A NOT gate is just two, one to 1 and one to 0.

Play with it yourself. It's free and open source: glassbox-production-fd52.up.railway.app/calculatorclear (link in bio)

youtubeLong.title: How does a calculator work? (interactive explainer)
youtubeLong.description:
Press 7 and a chip scans a grid of wires, waits out the bounce and stores 0111. Build the adder from real logic gates, watch the carry ripple, and see why 1 ÷ 3 × 3 can come out as 0.9999999.

▶ Play with the interactive version: https://glassbox-production-fd52.up.railway.app/e/calculatorclear/
⌘ Source code (MIT): https://github.com/bdeeps/calculatorclear

In this video:
• A handful of parts. Open a pocket calculator and you find rubber keys with carbon pills, a circuit board with a grid of pads, one chip under a blob of black epoxy, an LCD, and a solar cell with a button cell for backup.
• Keys become bits. The 20 keys sit where 5 row wires cross 4 column wires.
• Switches that decide. Transistors are switches worked by electricity.
• Adding is XOR and AND. The sum bit of two bits is XOR and the carry is AND.
• Seven bars of liquid crystal. A decoder turns each 4-bit digit into 7 segment signals.
• Microwatts and the last digit. CMOS and LCDs need so little power that a stamp-sized solar cell in room light runs the calculator.

Glassbox opens one box a day: an interactive model of how something works, plus the code behind it.
